findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "validating", "unbalanced").
findings.evidence: Mistakes: validating a BST by comparing only a node with its children (pass min/max bounds down instead), inserting sorted data into an unbalanced BST (it becomes a linked list), and hitting recursion depth limits on skewed trees.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The traversal code uses a (value, left, right) tuple encoding that is never stated, so the call line is hard to read.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note such as "node = (value, left, right)" before the code.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "mechanism", "building").
findings.evidence: Mechanism: push appends the item and sifts up in O(log n); pop swaps the root with the last item and sifts down in O(log n); peek is O(1); building a heap from n items with heapify is O(n).
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "efficiently", "independent").
findings.evidence: Comparison: a heap gives the min or max quickly but is not sorted and cannot search efficiently (O(n)), while a BST gives ordered search in O(h) (O(log n) if balanced, O(n) if skewed) but no O(1) min peek. A trie lookup costs O(L) in key length, independent of the number of keys.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "forgetting", "treating").
findings.evidence: Mistakes: forgetting that Python's heapq is only a min-heap (push negated values for a max-heap), treating the heap array as sorted, and omitting is_end so that 'app' wrongly matches when only 'apple' was inserted. Tries also cost a lot of memory.
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The trie node field is called `children[char]` in the notes but `node.kids` in the code, so the same thing has two names.
findings.evidence: "Trie node: children[char] + is_end; one char per step" vs "node = node.kids.setdefault(ch, Node())"
findings.fix: Use one name, such as `children`, in both the bullet and the code.

findings.summary: Kahn's algorithm is named in the mechanism flow and complexity bullet without ever being defined or tied to the topological sort definition.
findings.evidence: Definitions list only "Topological sort" and "Dijkstra"; later "Kahn's is O(V+E); fewer than V output = cycle"
findings.fix: Add a definition bullet such as "Kahn's: topological sort by repeatedly removing indegree-0 nodes" and label the flow "Kahn's algorithm".
